traceability.notes:
docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md is clearly a concrete specification with detailed acceptance criteria and requirements, so it qualifies as a story to assess. Most of the story’s scope is implemented: auto-fix for missing @story on functions/methods (REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING), safe suffix-only normalization of @story paths (REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT, REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE, REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE), configurable templates (REQ-AUTOFIX-TEMPLATE), selective auto-fix toggles (REQ-AUTOFIX-SELECTIVE), integration with existing validation rules, and user-facing documentation. These are all backed by rule implementations, helper modules, API reference documentation, and passing Jest tests (notably tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts).
However, two requirements and their corresponding acceptance criteria remain unimplemented with no concrete evidence in code or tests: - REQ-AUTOFIX-IDEMPOTENT / 'Idempotent Fixes' acceptance criterion. - REQ-AUTOFIX-SINGLE-APPLICATION / 'No Duplicate Fixes' acceptance criterion.
The story itself lists these acceptance criteria as unchecked ([ ]), and there are no traceability annotations, tests, or documentation explicitly covering idempotent behavior or guarantees against duplicate placeholder insertion. While the current fixers may, in practice, be idempotent and non-duplicating, this cannot be treated as implemented without explicit tests or documented guarantees. Because at least these two requirements are not demonstrably satisfied, the story as a whole is not fully implemented and the assessment status is FAILED.
